scope: Prospective finite search for fresh synthetic development conditions. All implementation, panel creation, historical overlap checks, FIT and DEV execution require a later authorization. The Dutch and London DEV estimands, numerical budgets, panel sizes, precision thresholds and any H2 hierarchy are defined in registration.json.

units.L: Integral of normalized service deficit over the full frozen horizon, in service seconds. Smaller is better.
units.person: Occupied person-seconds under the inherited native measure.
units.clock: Original T4c public 60 s decision clock, physical step and 3600 s horizon.
units.candidate: One formally emitted immutable policy descriptor in one arm, round and slot.
units.fit_position: One labelled (arm, round, slot, paired FIT condition) evaluation on the original facility entry point.
units.object_bytes: For newly specified semantic objects: JSON, UTF-8, sorted keys, no insignificant whitespace, ensure_ascii=true, allow_nan=false, no BOM or terminal newline; SHA-256 of those bytes, lowercase hex. A retained file reference hashes its actual saved bytes and records byte length. Historical input encodings are specified separately.

parent.identity: Rebuild/verify the public member list from the freeze and call the original worker. Its independently enforced plant gate, local automatic protection, person and tool limits, public prior, fees, clock and score stay bound to their original definitions.

O.initial_policy: parent with all six allowance indices zero
O.improvement: The fixed ordinary search makes new candidate policies around its own current incumbent. Paid FIT feedback may change the incumbent. The proposal program, contest, feedback interface and selector are held byte-identical across all rounds.

R.initial_policy: parent with all six allowance indices zero
R.improvement: Uses O's catalogue, initial program, incumbent update, FIT interface, selector, fixed deterministic scheduler and registration caps. Only the proposal program may replace its root production using the bounded feedback rewrite below. The meta-rule itself is frozen.

descriptive.meaning: No elective dispatch; native automatic protection active.
Original transparent direct rule from T4a.

arms.common_comparison: FIT baseline uses the original parent for both arms on exactly the same FIT conditions. R1 formal proposals must match in ordered descriptor bytes. After both child policies lock, one predeclared paired DEV pass scores the seven roles. Descriptive roles do not participate in search or the RSI contrast.

policy_language.encoding: Descriptor bytes are the canonical JSON array of six integer level indices in cell order. The policy ID is SHA-256(object_bytes({design_sha256: SHA-256(actual design.json bytes), parent_bundle_sha256: arms.parent.public_bundle_sha256, levels: descriptor})). The same descriptor is executed by the same frozen compiler and public worker in O and R; arm labels and search artifacts never enter the decision worker.
policy_language.parent_pass: Return the exact original response for the zero descriptor. For every other descriptor run the original parent first. Preserve its result if it has issued any request, if its rationale.reason differs from VALUE, or if it lacks a complete WAIT continuation. This preserves mandatory own review, renewals, unsupported posterior states and awaiting a paid result.
policy_language.admissible_choices: Use only entries already present in that parent's public continuation_table, with first=[subject,'A'], admitted_continuation_plans>0 and a fresh identical ALLOW from the original Gate.admit on the same public frame. No synthesis of requests or modification of action, permit, maintenance, evidence or duration. The separate native gate checks the selected request at issue. Failure of the repeated check cannot issue the work.

evidence_bin.DIRECT: The subject's current original onsite paid I is actionable under the original gate.each_read and gate.actionable, arrived<=now<until, or its latest arrived original fixed meter sample for that subject is unexpired and bad. For fixed readings use the latest sampled time among arrived readings, require meter/<subject> as source, and treat conflicting values at that time as unknown. A copy adds no signal. Select DIRECT before checking ALARM.
evidence_bin.ALARM: An original live alarm from gate.live(view,'alarm') covers this subject via the frozen public alarm_and_work route and its ordinary arrival guard. A board-wide alert uses the original public routing. A signed order is still required.
evidence_bin.ORDER: Remaining eligible admitted choices with a live signed original order. The alarm may be absent. Predicted service gain is required in every bin. No retrospective fault or deadline enters any bin.

slack_bin.definition: For each admitted request use t=view.time, finish=request.planned_end and a=finish+pub.latency. Let q be the largest until of current original open orders for this subject. Compute slack=min(q-t, subject.write_window[1]-finish, end_of_worker_shift-finish, 3600-a). This is remaining PUBLIC scheduling slack at issue. The gate retains its own strict endpoint checks.

policy_language.choice: For the WAIT branch w and admissible A branch b, gain=w.vector[0]-b.vector[0] and extra=max(0,b.vector[3]-w.vector[3]); indices 0 and 3 are the parent's expected service loss and priced combined loss. Retain b iff its cell's allowance>0, gain>0 and extra<=allowance. Use original finite binary64 values, no fit or hindsight at dispatch. Among retained branches minimize (-gain,extra,slack,index in pub.routes,subject identifier), comparing identifiers by ASCII. Return its unchanged Gate.admit request. If none remain, return the parent response. Preserve the public certificate and refusal fields; a changed decision's rationale records the chosen task, original WAIT and supporting public references.
policy_language.rationale_for_levels: At the parent's lambda=1, its original issue fee of 30 person-seconds has the same priced value as 30 service seconds. The grid allows one, two or four such fee units of extra predicted combined loss when public service loss decreases. Zero disables the exception. These settings were chosen from the public cost and clock.
policy_language.conformance_before_any_fit: A future separately authorized implementation must demonstrate, on public engineering-only fixtures, original parent/all-zero identical response bytes, pass-through for non-VALUE waits and mandatory tasks, legality at expiry, rejection on copied/stale evidence, treatment symmetry, one fixture per reachable bin and exact replay of the enumerator/ranker. Fixtures cannot supply FIT feedback or scientific outcomes.

ordinary_and_recursive_search.baseline_state: One all-zero incumbent with paired original-parent FIT score, empty formal proposal list, seen set containing its descriptor. Both start with exactly the same eligible candidates and state. No warm start, optimizer randomness, manual candidate, LLM, prior score or transferred code from incident work. Only the parent and the registered public contracts enter.
ordinary_and_recursive_search.quantities: The ordered trials, number of rounds, proposals per round K, FIT panel and both equal CPU ceilings come exclusively from registration.json. Require at least two rounds for a next-round witness and total formal emissions per arm <=4095. Both arms receive the same precommitted FIT conditions and the same clock/quota policy.

ordinary_state: current incumbent descriptor and its paid score
state_separation.mutable_program_R_only: Root of the proposal AST. Valid values are the base program and the twelve literal emit_then macros defined below (six cells times two signed directions). Its productions are executable proposal rules. Retain the installed before/after AST in full. The encoder rejects any other cell ordering, composition, branch, step or numeric weight.

ordinary_and_recursive_search.base_enumeration: In round r numbered from 1, visit all 4096 descriptors. Exclude the incumbent and the arm's seen descriptor identities structurally before emission, retaining exclusion counts/digests. Let cell order rotate the six registered cells left by (r-1) mod 6. For descriptor y about incumbent x, order by ascending (count of coordinates changed, sum of absolute level-index differences, tuple of changed cell positions in rotated order, tuple of all six level indices of y in rotated order). Changed positions are listed ascending. This is a total order. The fixed base program emits the first K descriptors. Structural catalogue visits never call a facility or scorer.

macro_production.substitution: The credited single-cell edit has cell c and signed direction d=sign(candidate[c]-starting_incumbent[c]) in {-1,+1} level-index units. Its companion m has the same evidence bin and opposite NEAR/FAR time bin: DIRECT_NEAR / DIRECT_FAR, ALARM_NEAR / ALARM_FAR, ORDER_NEAR / ORDER_FAR. c,m,d are placeholders in the literal AST template. Store concrete cells and signed integer steps in the retained program.
macro_production.semantics: Every production starts anew at the SAME next-round incumbent. First propose a simultaneous signed one-level edit to the credited and companion coordinates. Next propose a one-level transfer to the companion alone. Then propose a one-level continuation on the credited coordinate alone. Do not clip an out-of-range coordinate: skip that whole individual production and record its reason. Append the inherited base stream, suppress already-seen or same-round duplicates stably before formal issuance, and take exactly the first K eligible descriptors. The three rules construct candidate descriptors and share O's score, rank and policy catalogue. Retain each production's emission/skip and whether a later base duplicate was suppressed. All structural work counts toward the arm's CPU cap.

ordinary_and_recursive_search.feedback: After all slots of a round close, deliver one signed FIT packet per candidate and the starting incumbent's paid baseline to that arm. Expose candidate identity, expected/observed condition counts, completion status, summed L microseconds, summed person microseconds and total hard violations only. Compute each metric as the exact decimal value of its original unrounded numeric JSON token times 1e6 rounded half to even for each condition, then sum integers. Retain the original scores with the evaluator. Equal FIT weights and one fixed panel apply throughout. Do not expose identities of individual conditions, families, traces, peer packets or DEV. A missing/nonfinite required return is not a zero.
ordinary_and_recursive_search.selector: Require complete paired FIT coverage and zero hard violations for a promotable policy. Rank eligible candidates by (sum L microseconds, sum person microseconds, six-index descriptor in the registered cell order). A candidate may replace the incumbent only with a strictly smaller L sum. If none qualifies, keep the incumbent. Ties at the incumbent's L always retain the incumbent. Byte-identical descriptors share a policy identity, and scores do not establish policy identity.
ordinary_and_recursive_search.rewrite: After incumbent selection but comparing to the starting incumbent, find all complete zero-violation paid single-cell edits with strictly smaller L sum than that incumbent. Rank them with the same frozen selector. For a nonterminal R round, the first such candidate supplies the credited cell, signed direction, paid slot/receipt and exact L difference. Compile and install the literal three-production macro for that cell and direction. If there is no witness, keep the program. If the compiled program already exists, record a no-op. O receives the same shape of packet and computes the same evidence/credit audit but retains base byte-for-byte. In the terminal round, both retain the program and lock the incumbent after selection. No outgoing proposal is fabricated.
ordinary_and_recursive_search.barrier: Hash and time-seal the complete ordered list before releasing any score from that round. A condition/slot cannot serve the next round before the packet barrier. The evaluator releases no rank-ordered previews, partial results, timing channel by individual condition, or cross-arm feedback. DEV seed release and input creation occur only after both terminal policy and implementation envelopes are committed.
ordinary_and_recursive_search.duplicates_and_failures: Known descriptor repeats are removed by the common structural rule before issuance with counts and digest of the excluded set. Cross-arm duplicates are physically evaluated under each arm's own budget, as are distinct descriptors with coincident FIT actions/scores. No behavioural pre-screen on old trajectories. Reserve each formal proposal and its entire FIT block before validation. A post-commit duplicate, invalid compiler output, timeout, partial/missing score or resource breach remains charged as reserved; record actual starts, completions and CPU, close the paired barrier INCOMPLETE and retain unrun suffixes. No replacement, free retry, borrowed slot, or best available lockout. A completely measured hard violation is recorded as such and makes that candidate ineligible. Shared parent baseline is executed once per FIT condition; both arms reference the whole baseline, and physical totals count it once. Broken baseline or required safety/cost record prevents lock.
ordinary_and_recursive_search.cost_accounting: Per arm record logical candidate slots, reserved positions, physically launched/completed positions and actual process CPU, including proposal work; preserve attempts separately from unique slots. Fixed caps are identical, realized CPU may differ. CPU covers all charged worker descendants under the same per-arm accounting envelope; Slurm allocation and wall time are distinct. Instrumentation shared on behalf of both follows the symmetric rule in registration.json. Audit-only structural regeneration never calls a facility and supplies no search feedback.

round_evidence.representation: One immutable schema-validated record per arm per registered round, including stopped and unstarted rounds. Content-addressed sidecars are part of the evidence set; their bytes and lengths must be independently replayable and retained. A digest alone is insufficient. This registration pins the semantics only. A later authorized implementation must publish matching common executable/bundle, compiler, interpreter, selector, scoring adapter, sandbox and accounting identities before any FIT feedback; a substituted binary cannot enter an existing chain.
round_evidence.before: Commit input/output lineage, frozen code/grammar/interpreter/selector identity, pre-round AST bytes, starting incumbent bytes, seen-set bytes, resource envelope and actual ordered list including slot, descriptor, mutation cells, parent incumbent and membership exclusion commitment before FIT returns.
round_evidence.after: Retain original public/redacted FIT packet bytes and signed evaluator receipt, observed/expected coverage, validity/denials, visible score columns, ranking, accepted incumbent and its paid ancestry. Bind the specific credited paid slot, immutable reason, expected threshold and observed delta to the AST change. Save both AST blobs and a canonical patch. Patch is [] on identical bytes, otherwise exactly one RFC 6902 replace at empty JSON pointer with the new AST. Frozen interpreter and selector must match across all records.
round_evidence.next_round_witness: For a closed nonterminal round, a read-only auditor regenerates the next ordered K candidates twice using the same final incumbent, seen set, round number, caps and immutable interpreter. Change only the before versus after AST. Store both complete candidate lists, next-state commitment, ordered-difference flag and set-difference flag, and forward roster commitment in that record. Its successor links back, compares the actual pre-payment roster against the predicted after list and identifies which differing candidates were actually paid. This backward link avoids editing earlier immutable records. Auditor counterfactuals see no score/trajectory, cannot call a facility and never feed either search.
round_evidence.mechanism_report: Classify no-op, edited_with_identical_list, order_only and changed_membership separately. With a batch paid in full, reordering the same set provides no change of evaluated candidates. Mark actual proposal effect only when at least one differing descriptor is in the next paid batch. Trace that descriptor's paid slot and any successor incumbent by parent links to the final locked child. Report whether the changed search reached the selected policy; absent lineage stays unestablished. A changed child descriptor, digest, FIT score or DEV R-O point estimate alone cannot witness a change of improvement program. Report negative and null traces. None of these mechanism labels changes the numerical status of Q1-Q4.
round_evidence.missing: On unclosed rounds or a stop, preserve the entire scheduled slot roster, actual allocations/CPU and any partial evidence, mark unknown fields null with reason, mark later rounds UNRUN, and stop before DEV. A terminal CLOSED round has null next witness by design. Re-read locked child bytes, all AST transitions, packet signatures, evidence chain and actual next commitments independently before releasing the DEV batch.

access_control.stage0: No panel generation, hash queries against sealed datasets, facility calls, experiments or interface implementation. No H2 generation, read or derivation; no H3 intake. The planning auditor may read exactly the three pinned public T7 stage-1 development inputs named in registration.planning: comparison.json (including its rows to compute positive parts) and the two Slurm accounting tables. Search design receives aggregate planning figures, never the old row scores or positions as a search input. Other authoring inputs are the task and accepted public method contracts. There is no stage-2 outcome input to planning.

dispatch_worker_allow.nested_contract: Use only the version-pinned PUB_FIELDS, VIEW_FIELDS, FIELDS, SUBJECT_FIELDS, PROFILE_FIELDS, PAID_FIELDS, route keys and arrival validation in src/aegis_risk_dispatch/policy.py (SHA-256 f2c7974a167bc6f94de510d4a9dc78ddd04605e9b59c7b1c873d79e081d96810). Signed live permits, previous dispatches and nominal/actual work times must come through those existing fields. The bridge rejects extra keys, future arrivals and out-of-clock inputs and validates producer, type, exact public origin/copy metadata and permitted units. New scalar fields disguised as metadata are disallowed.

proposer_allow: this frozen DSL and program interpreter
public fixed resource caps and scheduling indices
own arm's committed descriptors, program and incumbent
own paid aggregate FIT packets in the exact feedback layout
fit_wire_fields: registered arm / round / slot or shared parent
sum occupied person time in integer microseconds
common batch receipt authenticating this fixed-layout packet

other_principals.new_panel_curator: After separate authorization, materializes the FIT batch, commits the exact split root and submits the single FIT overlap request. DEV uses its own registered one-time signed future randomness after both children lock; no DEV seed or inputs exist at FIT time. The curator then commits the single DEV batch before the independent DEV request. It keeps seed material, inputs and names outside developer mounts and cannot see H3 hash entries or FIT feedback.
other_principals.fit_evaluator: Reads only signed FIT inputs and its locked common facility/metric executable. Receives opaque descriptors, runs the parent and formal FIT slots, supplies only whitelisted packets. Its private plant state, fault times, outcomes and detailed accounting never flow to the dispatcher.
other_principals.dev_evaluator: A distinct evaluation principal receives the signed dual child lock and seven identities. DEV is created from future randomness only after that lock and released for scoring only after its own opaque PASS. The principal scores the immutable batch once and releases one complete result after closure.
other_principals.overlap_custodian: A separate controller administers the offline comparison principal and read-only sealed input-commitment index, including the historical H3 index. It shares no evaluator, development, Slurm or repository-writing credential and accepts exactly one authenticated fixed-batch request per split. It retains the opaque FIT input index for later DEV-versus-FIT comparison.
other_principals.auditor: Independent read-only principal verifies role access receipts, process/namespace manifest, ordered IPC/score digests, byte readbacks and clocks. It releases a signed bounded verdict and completeness report. No detailed protected data enters a developer chat, worktree, logs or shared storage.

denied: private physical state or plant/scoring objects in online or improvement workers
fault times, latent causes, scenario/evaluation labels, raw generator seeds or index-to-family maps
retrospective last opportunity/true deadline/best counterfactual action
future reports, unacknowledged paid samples and copied records treated as independent
historical trajectories/scores/row identities including H3; all H2 material
DEV performance or row identifiers during fit
cross-arm scores, shell/network/general repository access and mutable side inputs
enforcement_and_audit: Build minimum immutable per-role images from verified files. Start each under a distinct unprivileged identity, mount namespace and network-denied sandbox. Allow only declared read-only runtime/policy files, explicit pipes and its own append-only sink; drop other file descriptors, environment, history/caches, inherited credentials, host process inspection and shared scratch. A new directory, another agent or a Python audit hook alone cannot enforce this separation.

The broker type-checks both directions, tracks monotonically increasing frames, preserves origin, arrival, copies and order, and commits each permitted payload's schema/bytes/hash/time and producer/consumer. Use OS-level open/read/socket/process-denial accounting bound to executable, UID, image, mounts, process tree and stdout/stderr. Logs remain on the private server, with redacted signed counts returned.

Use future static/engineering negative-control probes for a denied file, prohibited IPC key and future record before releasing any real FIT; verify actual denial from the independent observer. Compare all successful reads to the whitelist and reconcile score releases to paid FIT slots, all launched jobs to Slurm and any DEV release to the dual lock. Missing audit coverage, an unexplained read/IPC or privileged cross-role access invalidates the affected experiment. Retain evidence, stop and request a fresh reviewed decision. Positive assurance requires these records, not a zero-filled declaration.

overlap_gate.stage: Prospective one-shot release gate PER SPLIT. FIT passes before any FIT score. DEV can be generated only after the dual policy lock using registered signed future randomness, and must pass its separate one-shot gate before any DEV score. Stage 0 only registers the procedure. H2 is never an input. The only later H3 input is its pre-existing sealed input commitment index within the independent controller.
historical_universe: T5 v1, v2, v3a, v3b and v3c, including FIT, DEV, fresh confirmation/extensions and any reused panels
overlap_gate.catalogue: Prior to submitting any candidate batch, the controller binds a versioned source inventory with publication/manifest root, complete expected cardinality, graph of explicitly reused panels and identity encoding for each entry. Archives claiming the same rows retain both aliases and verifiable parity. Gaps, truncation or incomparable projections for any prior required source give an indeterminate result. Do not treat an absent source or an unbuilt historical panel as empty without a signed zero-realization record.
overlap_gate.freshness: Precommit split RNG/derivation rules and sizes before FIT. Materialize each batch once when its registered randomness is available, commit its immutable full root before overlap submission, and keep private seed material and maps with the curator. For DEV the one-time signed future randomness is fixed after both children lock. Row labels or RNG namespaces alone cannot certify disjoint operative material. Scope any claim about numeric seed values to the actual derivation evidence: fingerprints compare realized inputs.

identities.full: SHA-256 of the historical canonical full input serialization. For the T5 lineage this is UTF-8 JSON with sort_keys=true, separators=(',',':'), ensure_ascii=true, allow_nan=false plus one LF. The curator computes the comparable full fingerprint for each registered legacy encoding and commits exact bytes.
identities.operative: For T4c/T5 v3-format and the pre-existing sealed H3 index take SHA-256 of sorted compact ASCII JSON without LF projected to {native,attachment,maintenance}, excluding outer labels, split and result metadata. Source is docs/mainline/t5-ordinary-improvement-development-v2/context_v2.py operative (file SHA-256 df6ccbf526742a07bb8bde20c83bf71595529af5ce5d0daadfd8daf037c1425e). For legacy T3 inputs without maintenance, additionally compare the common {native,attachment} projection on BOTH new and legacy sides with the symmetric signed-order normalization specified in panel-law.json (historical_catalogue.common_old_schema). Preserve the byte-exact original full identity and the separate v3 three-field identity with maintenance. Never add a sentinel/default only on one side. Account independently for any documented implicit default in each bound generator version. The evaluator and curator must bind the same core generator and interfaces to those projections.
identities.compatibility: The controller checks version/domain labels, cardinality, hash width and publication authenticity independently. Where a historical generator has a different executable interface, require its documented comparable frozen projection/commitments before a PASS. Generate the comparable projection from NEW inputs in the curator process, not from protected H3 rows. Never manufacture missing H3 commitments, open H3 rows, or substitute a file-level manifest digest for per-input comparison.

two_axes: FIT gate: for each hash kind count all duplicates within FIT (n minus distinct) and compare FIT against every required historical set, including sealed H3.
DEV gate: for each hash kind count all duplicates within DEV and compare DEV against the frozen FIT input index and every required historical set, including sealed H3.
Reused old-old identities give no permission for overlap with a new split. Registered twins may share visible histories or workforce profiles; their full and operative inputs must differ.
overlap_gate.non_oracle: Only one version-authenticated whole batch of the registered size and signed randomness per split may enter. Authenticate its single-use request bound to registration, split, batch root and complete old catalogue; the DEV request additionally binds the prior FIT index and dual lock. No developer-supplied probes, rowwise queries, subset tests, adaptive retries or timing/error responses by source. The controller privately records all exact checks, denominators and artifact roots. The outward signed receipt contains registration ID, split, opaque batch root, controller/auditor identity, opaque old catalogue root, aggregate coverage, all-required-tests-complete flag and one PASS or BLOCKED decision. No peer hash, matched identity, family, source-specific counts, old index or failure detail is returned to development roles.
overlap_gate.release: PASS requires complete, authenticated, comparable full AND operative coverage and zero for every required intersection and within-split duplicate under both identities. Collision, incomparable or missing commitments, corrupted/unauthenticated bytes, or invalid access controls return the same opaque BLOCKED. Preserve batch, current locks, already completed earlier work and private evidence; keep the affected split unscored. No repair, replacement, re-query, adaptive resampling or H3 inspection in the attempt. The signed receipt itself can be verified again without querying input sets. Any investigation or revised protocol requires a separate decision outside this attempt.
